newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ household savings rise 3.5 pct in Dec qtr - bank.
newsitem.headline: NZ household savings rise 3.5 pct in Dec qtr - bank.

text.p: The December quarter saw a 3.5 percent rise in the net worth of New Zealand households, giving a healthy 9.5 percent annual increase, Westpac Investment Management said on Monday.

"New Zealand households have experienced a dramatic jump in savings at a time when it is still a common belief that New Zealanders have a poor savings record," said David Beattie, chief investment officer of Westpac Investment Management.
He said December quarter Westpac/FPG Household Savings Indicators showed New Zealand households were in a better position than they had been for some time.
Deposits held at financial institutions rose 8.5 percent in the quarter, compared to a more modest five percent rise in other financial assets.
The value of housing assets rose 2.2 percent over the quarter.
Beattie said a 9.6 percent rise in the value of household share investments was considerably helped by the 7.8 percent rise in the New Zealand share market.
There was a 6.5 percent fall in the amount of money invested in unit trusts and group investment funds in the quarter.
"Overall, this quarter's large increase in household net worth was driven by the large increase in bank deposits and very good returns from New Zealand bond and share markets," Beattie said.
"Increased house prices and a slowdown in the annual rate of change of borrowing also assisted."

Beattie said the rise in household net worth was encouraging news in view of the current retirement savings debate. The 15.5 percent annual rise in net worth, excluding housing assets and mortgage liabilities, was the largest annual rise in the six years of available data.

"At a time when it is still a commonly-held belief that New Zealand has a poor savings record, increases of this magnitude should at least suggest that New Zealanders may, in fact, be heeding the messages and have begun to act, voluntarily," Beattie said.
A public referendum on a compulsory retirement savings scheme, proposed by the government's junior coalition partner New Zealand First, has been scheduled for September.
